title: Chirality as Single-Measurement Discriminator for Extraterrestrial Common Ancestry
author: Avi Loeb (Harvard / Galileo Project)

layer_assignment.rationale: All claims rest on peer-reviewed data (OSIRIS-REx Bennu sample analysis, published amino acid racemization studies, established chirality physics). The speculative element ('interstellar gardener') is framed as philosophical follow-up, not empirical claim. Mirror-life biosafety concern is policy-level extrapolation from known biochemistry.

key_claims.statement: Chirality (handedness of DNA/RNA and amino acids) is the cleanest single-measurement discriminator between three hypotheses for shared biochemistry with extraterrestrial life: shared ancestry, convergent chemistry, or directed panspermia.
key_claims.empirical_status: Testable in principle; no ET sample yet available

key_claims.statement: OSIRIS-REx Bennu sample analysis reveals amino acids are racemic (equal L/R mix), contradicting prior theories that space-formed amino acids naturally favor L-handedness.
key_claims.empirical_status: Published; 121.6g sample; 14/20 terrestrial amino acids + all 5 nucleobases confirmed

key_claims.statement: Mirror-image bacteria would evade innate immune recognition, resist standard antibiotics, and pose existential biosafety risks if released.
key_claims.empirical_status: No mirror bacteria created; policy argument in Science Forum; supported by chiral recognition biochemistry

key_claims.statement: If multiple extraterrestrial life samples share Earth's chirality AND nucleobase set, the urgent question becomes origin-of-origin: 'Who created us all?'
key_claims.empirical_status: No ET sample available; framing question, not empirical claim

pattern_resonance.description: The 'single measurement' principle (chirality as minimal observable) mirrors the A_c framework's core design goal: find the minimal set of observables that distinguish random from non-random structure. Loeb's three-hypothesis decision tree (shared ancestry / convergent chemistry / directed panspermia) is structurally isomorphic to the Cloud-9 four-layer discrimination problem.
